title: Four different teams, the same underlying answer: deterministic policy, outside the model

children.title: Meta, LlamaFirewall (Purple Llama, real, arXiv 2505.03574)
lines: PromptGuard 2 (jailbreak detector) → Agent Alignment Checks (a chain-of-thought auditor reading the agent's own reasoning for goal misalignment) → CodeShield (static analysis before generated code executes).
Scope: content-safety, not authorization, answers "is this dangerous," not "is this agent allowed."

children.title: OpenAI, tool approvals + moderation pipeline
lines: Separates prompt from tool execution; a synchronous moderation layer screens input/output before a tool call is even generated; human-in-the-loop approval is the default for higher-risk actions.
See the real July 2026 incident below, even this didn't stop a benchmark exploit chain.

children.title: Google, Vertex AI / Agent Development Kit
lines: Tool calls are matched deterministically against a pre-defined OpenAPI schema: a call that doesn't exactly match the schema is rejected by the API gateway itself, not by asking the model to reconsider.
Same shape as a well-built capability gate: the schema/policy check is code, not a second model call.

children.title: AWS, Bedrock AgentCore (2025)
lines: AgentCore Identity brokers short-lived, per-agent STS credentials (AssumeRole + a per-call session policy) instead of a standing IAM role; AgentCore Gateway sits in front of every tool call, evaluated against Cedar, AWS's own deterministic, formally-verified policy language.

children.title: The pattern every one of them converges on
lines: 1. A short-lived, per-agent credential, never a standing role or a secret shared across every agent instance.
2. The identity is resolved server-side, from the credential, never trusted from what the agent's own output claims to be.
3. The allow/deny decision is deterministic code (Rego, Cedar, an OpenAPI schema match), not a second model asked to judge the first one's tool call.
4. Content-safety scanners (PromptGuard/CodeShield-style) are a SEPARATE, complementary layer, never a substitute for the authorization decision above.

children.title: A platform combining short-lived per-agent keys, server-side header re-stamping, and a deterministic policy gate is a working instance of the same shape.
